samples.summary: Row/column reorder is refused whenever ANY merged block straddles the freeze, even one the move does not touch
samples.evidence: `moveCells` builds `movedMerges = moveMergeMap(this.merges, axis, src, count, dst)` and refuses if *any* entry crosses the pane. A block that already straddled before the move (legacy document, XLSX/seed import, or a CRDT race where peer A freezes while peer B merges) is still straddling in `movedMerges`, so every reorder — including a *column* reorder when the straddle is on the row axis, and reorders of rows nowhere near the block — returns `false` with `refuse('merge-move-frozen')`. The guard should compare against the pre-move state (refuse only blocks that *newly* straddle), not the absolute post-move map. Same defect in the backend copy: `worksheet-structure.controller.ts:193-203` throws a 409 (`The move would leave the merged range anchored at ...`) for a pre-existing straddler, so `POST .../move` is permanently blocked on such a document.

samples.summary: snapFreezePastMerges grows the freeze without any bound, so freezing one row can freeze tens of thousands of rows and make the tab unpaintable
samples.evidence: `rows = range[1].r` snaps the boundary to the bottom of any block it cuts, with no ceiling. A merge of up to 100000 cells is explicitly allowed (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:23` MaxMergedCells), and merging is only refused when a freeze already exists. So: merge `A1:A100000` with freeze 0 (allowed by `canMergeSelection` and by `PUT merges`), then freeze 1 row — `Sheet.setFreezePane` (sheet.ts:533) and `PUT .../freeze` (worksheet.controller.ts:112) both store frozenRows=100000. `view/layout.ts:149` computes `frozenHeight = rowDim.getOffset(frozenRows + 1)` and the frozen pane paints every frozen row — the exact 'UI never paints, and the user cannot reach the freeze menu to undo it' failure `parseFreeze`'s bound was written to prevent. The same snap now also fires unconditionally on every insert/delete via `shiftWorksheetViewState` (worksheet-structure.ts:278) and `Sheet.shiftCells` (sheet.ts:1418), so a legacy document with a tall block starting inside the frozen band gets this applied and persisted on the next structural edit.

samples.summary: revalidateCopyBuffer silently does nothing when the copied range has no axis anchors, leaving a stale index-keyed buffer after a remote structural edit
samples.evidence: `if (!buffer?.sourceAnchors) return;` — `anchorsForRange` (sheet.ts:2236) returns undefined whenever `refToAnchor` cannot resolve either corner, i.e. whenever the copied range sits past axis-ID coverage (a copy from an area below/right of the materialized rowOrder/colOrder, which is common on a sparse sheet). The buffer then survives a peer's insert/delete/reorder, and because the view paste paths no longer clear the buffer at all (view/worksheet.ts:4953, view/spreadsheet.ts:728), a later paste relocates formulas and now re-creates merged blocks from renumbered, stale coordinates — the exact failure this function exists to prevent. Falling back to clearing (or recording an index fallback) would close it.

samples.summary: The merge-split branch of moveCells still returns silently with no refusal notice, while the new view code now also suppresses the selection update
samples.evidence: `moveCells` returns `false` for `isMergeSplitByMove` without calling `this.refuse('merge-source-split')`, unlike the freeze branch three lines below which does refuse. The new drag handler (`view/worksheet.ts:4661-4666`) bails on `!moved`, so a drag-reorder that would split a merged block now produces no message, no selection change and no render — a completely silent no-op. The comment there claims 'is refused', which is only true for the frozen case.

samples.summary: The freeze snap runs on every shift, including shifts that change neither the boundary nor any block's relation to it, silently rewriting legacy documents
samples.evidence: `snapFreezePastMerges` is called unconditionally at the end of `shiftWorksheetViewState` (and in `Sheet.shiftCells:1418`) rather than only when the shift moved the boundary or a block across it. On a document that already contains a straddling block — reachable from older documents or a concurrent freeze/merge — an insert or delete far from both the freeze and the block will grow `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` and persist the change, with the v1 insert/delete response not reporting it (the caller must re-`GET .../freeze` to notice).

finding.summary: Row/column reorder is refused whenever ANY merged block straddles the freeze, even one the move does not touch

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described. sheet.ts:1552-1558 builds `movedMerges = moveMergeMap(this.merges, axis, src, count, dst)` and refuses with `refuse('merge-move-frozen')` if ANY entry in the post-move map crosses the pane, with no comparison to the pre-move state. `moveMerge` (merging.ts:103-137) only remaps the moved axis, so a block straddling the row freeze survives unchanged through a column reorder and still trips `crossesFreezePane` (merging.ts:184-194) — refusing reorders the move never touched. The backend copy at worksheet-structure.controller.ts:181-204 has the identical absolute-map loop and throws a 409. I looked for a guard making a pre-existing straddler unreachable and found none: `loadFreezePane`/`loadMerges` (sheet.ts:556-580, reused at 5368-5369 and view/worksheet.ts:432-433, 5233-5234) load both fields verbatim without snapping, and `migrateLegacyWorksheet` (worksheet-shape-migration.ts:444,449) copies `merges` and `frozenRows/frozenCols` across with no snap; nothing re-validates after remote CRDT convergence, so a concurrent freeze+merge leaves a straddler no path repairs. The codebase's own precedent (setFreezePane sheet.ts:532-537, shiftCells sheet.ts:1418-1428, applyWorksheetShift worksheet-structure.ts:276-281) snaps the boundary instead of refusing, confirming the move path's handling of a pre-existing straddler is the odd one out. Impact: all row/column reorders permanently refused in the editor and a permanent 409 on POST .../move for such a document — major, in the correctness lane (wrong condition / broken invariant handling).

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: snapFreezePastMerges (merging.ts:212-232) grows `rows`/`cols` to the far edge of any straddling merge with no ceiling and no clamp anywhere in the repo. The path is reachable: parseMerges (worksheet-settings.ts:140-152) accepts a single merge of up to 100000 cells (e.g. A1 rs=100000, cs=1), and assertMergesClearOfFreeze (worksheet.controller.ts:189) returns early when the tab has no freeze, so the tall block is stored; a subsequent PUT freeze {rows:1} passes parseFreeze and stores snapped.frozenRows = 100000 (worksheet.controller.ts:112-119). Sheet.setFreezePane (sheet.ts:532-536) does the same in the editor, and sheet.ts:1418-1428 / worksheet-structure.ts:278 re-apply it on every structural edit. The render impact is confirmed: buildFreezeState (view/layout.ts:145-152) does not clamp, and the frozen quadrants iterate rows 1..frozenRows every frame (gridcanvas.ts:329-332 and 400-405 into renderQuadrantCells -> buildTextOverflowRenderData/buildRenderableRefs at gridcanvas.ts:598-615); ctx.clip() bounds pixels, not iterations. I found no guard, caller-side check, or clamp that makes this unreachable, so I have no named ground to refute.
